completed_tasks.name: 07-02 Neutral DatasetStore extraction (storage.datasets, storage.fs, storage.onelake_fs, storage.locking)

blockers.description: Fundamental design shift: Fabric is to become the unified data platform — Fabric pipelines own ingestion/refresh from ARG, LAW, and other sources, plus data cataloguing and ETL to curate all tables needed by web/API/Hermes. Every component becomes a consumer of Fabric-curated data; no component (including Hermes/API) queries ARG/LAW directly anymore. User explicitly accepted the consequence that Fabric's ARG connector is import-only (no DirectQuery, typically 15+ min refresh latency) and chose to accept minutes of staleness everywhere, including previously-interactive features like live network path analysis.
blockers.workaround: Phase 7 plans 03-06 assume Python (the new intelligence/inventory domain) issues its own ARG query for PaaS acquisition (D-15) and owns acquisition/normalization/retention/publication in-process (D-01/D-02). Under the new model, acquisition/ETL belongs in Fabric pipelines, not Python. These plans need to be re-scoped or rewritten against the new architecture before further execution.

human_actions_pending.action: Design the Fabric-as-unified-data-platform shift: define which Fabric pipelines ingest which sources (ARG, LAW, others), the cataloguing/ETL layer, the curated tables each consumer (web, API, Hermes) needs, and how the existing FABRIC_INTEGRATION.md model (Fabric as projection, Azure as source of truth) is superseded or revised.
human_actions_pending.context: This is an architecture-level reversal of the currently documented principle in FABRIC_INTEGRATION.md ("Fabric is the governed semantic and analytics plane... not the source of operational truth"). It should probably be captured as a new roadmap phase or a revision to PROJECT.md/ROADMAP.md before Phase 7 plans are touched again.

decisions.decision: Pause Phase 7 (Unified Resource Inventory) after plan 02; do not execute 07-03 through 07-06 as currently written.
decisions.rationale: Those plans' premise (Python/inventory domain queries ARG directly and owns the ETL) is superseded by the new Fabric-as-unified-platform direction.

decisions.decision: 07-02's neutral extraction (storage.datasets.DatasetStore, storage.fs, storage.onelake_fs, storage.locking) is believed to survive the pivot.
decisions.rationale: Generic OneLake publish/read plumbing is still needed by whatever writes/reads Fabric-curated tables, regardless of who performs ingestion.

decisions.decision: Under the new model, all consumers (web, API, Hermes) read only Fabric-curated data; no direct ARG/LAW queries from Python, even for interactive/live features.
decisions.rationale: User explicit choice after being told Fabric's ARG connector is import-only with ~15+ minute typical refresh latency — accepted the staleness tradeoff for a single unified data platform over per-component live queries.

decisions.decision: Subscription differentiation in Fabric is handled by row-level tagging only (subscription_id/tenant_id columns on every curated table, already present per dataset_mapper.py) — Fabric/OneLake does not need to enforce access isolation itself.
decisions.rationale: User chose row-tagging + existing API-layer authorization over Fabric-side RLS/per-tenant workspaces, matching today's model where the API already scopes which subscriptions a connection/user can query.
